title: Tainan Trains Go Underground as Historic Station Gets New Role
summaryZh: 台南鐵路地下化首段週六通車，百年台南車站將保留並轉型。
summaryHi: तैनान में शनिवार से ट्रेनें भूमिगत चलेंगी, ऐतिहासिक स्टेशन को नई भूमिका मिलेगी।
summaryEs: Los trenes de Tainan pasan bajo tierra y la histórica estación tendrá nuevos usos.
summaryJa: 台南の鉄道地下化第1段階が土曜に開業、歴史ある駅は新たな役割へ。
summaryKo: 타이난 철도 지하화 첫 구간이 토요일 개통하고 역사적 역은 새 역할을 맡는다.
summaryEn: Tainan's trains move underground, and the historic station will get new uses.
paragraphs: Trains in the southern city of Tainan will start running underground on Saturday, marking the completion of the first 8.23-kilometre stage of a long-awaited railway project. According to the Ministry of Transportation and Communications, the new section will eliminate 23 level crossings, easing traffic bottlenecks and making streets safer for pedestrians and cyclists.

The project, approved by the Cabinet in 2009, has proved more costly than expected, with its budget rising from NT$33 billion to NT$41.26 billion. Part of the delay came from archaeology: the city's Cultural Affairs Bureau identified 20 sites containing remains from prehistoric times to the Japanese colonial period, and investigating them added roughly two years. Full completion is now scheduled for March 2031.
Once the old tracks are removed, the corridor they occupy will be turned into a greenway about 30 metres wide, with paths for walking and cycling.

The historic Tainan Station, which opened in 1900 and was rebuilt in 1936, will remain in use beside the new underground station, connected to it by a sunken plaza. Taiwan Railway Corp. is considering cafes, souvenir shops, reading spaces and exhibitions for the building. Chen Yen-chung, an urban planning professor at National Cheng Kung University, said the station could introduce visitors to the 400-year history of Taiwan's former capital.
Trains in the city of Tainan will start to run under the ground on Saturday. The new underground part of the railway is 8.23 kilometres long.
Before, cars and people had to stop at 23 places where the road crossed the railway. Now these crossings will go. This will help people who walk and ride bikes.
The work started many years ago. It is costing NT$41.26 billion. It will be finished in 2031. Later, the old railway land will become a long green park with paths.
Tainan Station is very old. It first opened in 1900. The old building will stay. A new station is next to it. The old building may have cafes, small shops and art shows.

Trains in Tainan, a city in southern Taiwan, will begin running underground on Saturday. The first underground section of the railway is 8.23 kilometres long, and the government says it will remove 23 level crossings.

Without these crossings, traffic should move more easily, and it will be safer for people on foot and on bicycles. After the old tracks are taken away, the land will become a green path about 30 metres wide for walking and cycling.

The Cabinet approved the project in 2009. Since then, the cost has gone up from NT$33 billion to NT$41.26 billion. One reason for the delay was archaeology: workers found 20 sites with very old remains, and this added about two years to the work. Everything should be finished in March 2031.

Tainan Station first opened in 1900, when Japan ruled Taiwan. The building we see today was built in 1936. It will stay next to the new underground station, and the railway company wants to fill it with cafes, shops, reading areas and exhibitions.

Trains in the southern city of Tainan will start running underground on Saturday, marking the completion of the first 8.23-kilometre stage of a long-awaited railway project. According to the Ministry of Transportation and Communications, the new section will eliminate 23 level crossings, easing traffic bottlenecks and making streets safer for pedestrians and cyclists.

The project, approved by the Cabinet in 2009, has proved more costly than expected, with its budget rising from NT$33 billion to NT$41.26 billion. Part of the delay came from archaeology: the city's Cultural Affairs Bureau identified 20 sites containing remains from prehistoric times to the Japanese colonial period, and investigating them added roughly two years. Full completion is now scheduled for March 2031.
Once the old tracks are removed, the corridor they occupy will be turned into a greenway about 30 metres wide, with paths for walking and cycling.

The historic Tainan Station, which opened in 1900 and was rebuilt in 1936, will remain in use beside the new underground station, connected to it by a sunken plaza. Taiwan Railway Corp. is considering cafes, souvenir shops, reading spaces and exhibitions for the building. Chen Yen-chung, an urban planning professor at National Cheng Kung University, said the station could introduce visitors to the 400-year history of Taiwan's former capital.

After more than a decade and a half of construction, trains in Tainan are set to disappear beneath the city on Saturday, when the first 8.23-kilometre underground stretch of the railway opens. Transport officials say the move will do away with 23 level crossings that have long divided neighbourhoods and choked traffic.

The scheme has not come cheap. First approved by the Cabinet in 2009, its price tag has swelled from NT$33 billion to more than NT$41 billion, partly because excavation uncovered 20 archaeological sites spanning prehistory, the Qing dynasty and the Japanese era. Preserving or relocating those remains pushed the schedule back by about two years, and the whole project is not due to be finished until 2031.
The land freed up by the removal of the tracks is earmarked for a greenway roughly 30 metres wide, giving residents a continuous route for walking and cycling through the old city.

Perhaps the most symbolic element is the fate of Tainan Station, a national monument rebuilt in 1936. Rather than being sidelined by a new terminal further north, it will stand alongside the underground station and be repurposed with cafes, exhibitions and reading spaces. Chen Yen-chung, an urban planning professor at National Cheng Kung University, argued that heritage rules should be regarded as an opportunity rather than a constraint.

Tainan, Taiwan's oldest city, is poised to reach a milestone in its urban transformation this Saturday, when trains begin operating along the first 8.23-kilometre underground section of its railway. The Ministry of Transportation and Communications anticipates that eliminating 23 level crossings will alleviate congestion and substantially improve accessibility for pedestrians and cyclists.

Nevertheless, the project illustrates the formidable challenges of large-scale infrastructure. Endorsed by the Cabinet in 2009, it has seen its budget escalate from NT$33 billion to NT$41.26 billion. Archaeological investigations, which revealed 20 sites with artefacts ranging from prehistoric times to the Japanese colonial era, extended the timetable by approximately two years, and full completion is not anticipated until March 2031.
Once the surface tracks have been dismantled, the vacated corridor will be transformed into a landscaped greenway approximately 30 metres wide, featuring dedicated walking and cycling paths.

Equally significant is the preservation of Tainan Station, which was rebuilt in 1936 and designated a national monument in 1998. Instead of being superseded by a new terminal, the historic building will be integrated with the underground station via a sunken plaza and adapted to accommodate cafes, exhibitions and reading areas. Academics contend that such heritage constraints, far from being limitations, could enable the station to serve as a gateway to the city's four centuries of history.

note.meaning: 艱鉅的、令人生畏的；（對手）難以對付的。
note.usage: 形容詞，常修飾 challenge / task / obstacle / opponent；可指困難巨大，也可指能力強大而令人敬畏。

example.en: Rebuilding the economy after the war was a formidable task.
example.zh: 戰後重建經濟是一項艱鉅的任務。

noteHi.meaning: अत्यंत कठिन या भयावह; (प्रतिद्वंद्वी) जिससे निपटना कठिन हो।
noteHi.usage: विशेषण; challenge / task / opponent के साथ आम। बड़ी कठिनाई या प्रभावशाली शक्ति दोनों दर्शा सकता है।
noteHi.exampleTr: युद्ध के बाद अर्थव्यवस्था का पुनर्निर्माण एक अत्यंत कठिन कार्य था।

noteEs.meaning: formidable en el sentido de enorme y difícil; temible.
noteEs.usage: Adjetivo con challenge / task / opponent. En inglés suele indicar dificultad o fuerza, no 'maravilloso'.
noteEs.exampleTr: Reconstruir la economía tras la guerra fue una tarea formidable.

noteJa.meaning: 手ごわい、非常に困難な；畏怖を感じさせる。
noteJa.usage: 形容詞で challenge / task / opponent などを修飾する。困難の大きさや相手の強さを表す。
noteJa.exampleTr: 戦後の経済再建は非常に困難な課題だった。

noteKo.usage: 형용사로 challenge / task / opponent 등을 수식. 어려움의 크기나 상대의 강함을 나타냄.
noteKo.exampleTr: 전후 경제 재건은 매우 어려운 과제였다.

noteEn.meaning: very difficult to deal with; impressive and a little frightening.

found.ex: Workers found old coins under the road.
found.zh: 發現；找到（find 的過去式）

freed.ex: The space freed by the old car park will become a garden.

from.en: starting at; showing origin or a starting point

full.ex: Full results will be announced on Friday.

further.en: at or to a greater distance
further.ex: The new market is further east than the old one.

gateway.en: a way of reaching or learning about something
gateway.ex: The port city is a gateway to the islands.

giving.ex: The new path runs along the river, giving cyclists a safe route.

go.en: to move or return somewhere; to disappear or be removed
go.ex: She wants to go back to school next year.

gone.ex: The price of rice has gone up again.

government.en: the group of people who rule a country
government.ex: The government will build more homes next year.

green.en: having many plants and trees; the colour of grass
green.ex: The city wants more green spaces for children.

greenway.en: a strip of land with trees and paths for walking and cycling
greenway.ex: We cycled along the greenway beside the river.

ground.ex: The pipes run deep under the ground.
ground.hi: ज़मीन; (under the ground) ज़मीन के नीचे

had.en: past of have; (had to) were required to
had.ex: We had to wait an hour for the bus.
had.ja: 〜しなければならなかった；持っていた

half.ex: The trip took a year and a half.
half.ja: 半分；（a decade and a half）15年
half.zh: 一半；（a decade and a half）十五年

has.en: possesses; also used to form perfect tenses
has.ex: The town has two parks and a library.

have.en: to possess or suffer from; also used to form perfect tenses
have.ex: Many children have colds in winter.

help.en: to make things easier for someone; (n.) assistance
help.ex: Volunteers help older people with shopping.

heritage.en: old buildings and traditions valued as part of history
heritage.ex: The old temple is part of the city's heritage.

historic.en: important in history; old and famous
historic.ex: We walked around the historic town centre.
historic.zh: 歷史悠久的；具歷史意義的

history.en: the past events of a place or people
history.ex: The city has a long and rich history.

identified.ex: Scientists identified a new type of bird.

illustrates.en: shows clearly or acts as an example of
illustrates.ex: This story illustrates the value of hard work.

improve.ex: Regular exercise can improve your sleep.

in.en: inside; during; within a place, time or group

infrastructure.en: basic systems and structures like roads, railways and buildings
infrastructure.ex: The country spent billions on roads and other infrastructure.

instead.es: en lugar de; en vez de
instead.ex: Instead of driving, she took the train.

integrated.en: combining different parts or services into one; joined together with
integrated.ex: The new station will be integrated with the bus terminal.
integrated.ja: 統合型の；一体化された
integrated.zh: 整合的；（be integrated with）與…相連

into.en: to the inside of; changing to become something

introduce.en: to help someone learn about something for the first time
introduce.ex: The guide will introduce visitors to the old town.
introduce.ja: 紹介する；知ってもらう

investigating.en: examining something carefully to find facts
investigating.ex: Investigating the old mine took several months.

investigations.ex: Police investigations into the fire are continuing.

is.ex: The museum is open every day except Monday.

japanese.en: of Japan (here, the Japanese colonial period in Taiwan)

kilometre.ex: The school is about one kilometre from my home.

kilometres.ex: The lake is five kilometres from the village.

kung.en: part of the name National Cheng Kung University

land.ex: The empty land will become a football field.

landscaped.en: designed with trees, grass and paths to look attractive
landscaped.ex: The hotel has a beautifully landscaped garden.

large-scale.en: involving many people, things or a large area
large-scale.ex: The city has started a large-scale cleaning project.

later.en: at a time after now or after that
later.ex: The shop will open later in the year.

level.en: (level crossing) a place where a road crosses a railway at the same height
level.ex: The car stopped at the level crossing as a train passed.

limitations.en: rules or facts that limit what can be done
limitations.ex: The plan has some limitations, but it is a good start.

long.en: measuring a great length; (adv.) for a long time
long.ex: The bridge is two kilometres long.

long-awaited.en: hoped for or expected for a long time
long-awaited.ex: The long-awaited film finally opens this Friday.

making.ex: The new lights are making the park safer at night.

march.en: the third month of the year
march.ex: The new school term begins in March.

marking.en: showing that an important event has happened
marking.ex: The concert was held in June, marking the town's 100th birthday.

may.en: used to say something is possible
may.ex: The old shop may become a small cafe.

metres.ex: The river is about fifty metres wide here.

milestone.en: an important stage or event in development
milestone.ex: Finishing the first bridge was a milestone for the city.

note.meaning: 里程碑；重要的階段或轉折點。
note.usage: 可數名詞，常用 reach / mark / pass a milestone；a milestone in + 名詞（某領域或過程中的里程碑）。

example.en: Launching the satellite was a milestone in the country's space programme.
example.zh: 發射這顆衛星是該國太空計畫的一個里程碑。

noteHi.meaning: मील का पत्थर; किसी प्रक्रिया का महत्वपूर्ण चरण।
noteHi.usage: गणनीय संज्ञा: reach / mark a milestone; a milestone in + संज्ञा।
noteHi.exampleTr: उपग्रह का प्रक्षेपण देश के अंतरिक्ष कार्यक्रम में एक मील का पत्थर था।

noteEs.usage: Sustantivo contable: reach / mark a milestone; a milestone in + sustantivo.
noteEs.exampleTr: El lanzamiento del satélite fue un hito en el programa espacial del país.

noteJa.meaning: 画期的な出来事、重要な節目。
noteJa.usage: 可算名詞。reach / mark a milestone、a milestone in ～ の形が多い。
noteJa.exampleTr: その衛星の打ち上げは同国の宇宙計画における画期的な出来事だった。

noteKo.usage: 가산 명사. reach / mark a milestone, a milestone in + 명사 형태가 흔함.
noteKo.exampleTr: 그 위성 발사는 그 나라 우주 계획의 이정표였다.

noteEn.meaning: an important event or stage in a process.
noteEn.usage: Countable; often 'reach / mark a milestone' or 'a milestone in + noun'.

ministry.ex: The ministry released new rules for schools.

monument.en: a historic building or site that is officially protected
monument.ex: The old temple is protected as a national monument.

more.en: a greater number of; to a greater degree (more easily, more costly)

most.en: to the greatest degree (the most + adjective)
most.ex: This is the most beautiful beach on the island.

move.en: an action taken to achieve something (n.); to go from place to place (v.)
move.ex: Cutting bus fares was a popular move.

national.ex: The team won the national championship last year.

neighbourhoods.en: areas of a town where people live
neighbourhoods.ex: The new road connects two quiet neighbourhoods.

nevertheless.en: despite what has just been said
nevertheless.ex: It was raining; nevertheless, the match went ahead.

new.ex: The city opened a new library downtown.

north.ex: We drove north for three hours.

not.en: used to make a statement negative
not.ex: The museum is not open on Mondays.

now.ex: The shop is now closed for the holiday.

occupy.en: to fill or use a space
occupy.ex: The new offices occupy two floors of the building.

of.en: belonging to; showing a part or amount

officials.en: people with positions of authority in government
officials.ex: City officials will announce the results tomorrow.

old.en: having existed for a long time; of advanced age (old age)
old.ex: The old bridge will be closed next month.

oldest.en: having existed for the longest time
oldest.ex: This is the oldest church in the country.

on.en: used for days (on Thursday) and states (on the rise, on foot)

opened.en: started to operate for the first time

opens.en: starts to operate or be used
opens.ex: The new museum opens next week.

operating.ex: The ferry stopped operating during the storm.

opportunity.en: a chance to do something good
opportunity.ex: The job is a great opportunity to travel.

park.en: a public area of grass and trees
park.ex: Children play football in the park after school.

part.en: a piece or section of something larger
part.ex: This part of the city is very quiet.

partly.en: to some extent but not completely
partly.ex: The delay was partly caused by bad weather.

path.en: a narrow way for walking or cycling
path.ex: A narrow path leads down to the beach.

paths.en: narrow ways for walking or cycling
paths.ex: The park has paths for runners and cyclists.

pedestrians.ex: This street is closed to cars and open to pedestrians.

people.ex: Many people visit the market on Sundays.

perhaps.ex: Perhaps the best part of the trip was the food.

period.en: a length of time in history
period.ex: The house was built during the colonial period.

places.ex: There are many places to eat near the station.

planning.en: the work of designing how a city or area develops
planning.ex: She studied city planning at university.

plaza.en: an open public square in a town
plaza.ex: People gathered in the plaza to watch the show.

poised.en: ready and about to do something
poised.ex: The team is poised to win its first title.

note.meaning: 準備就緒的、即將（做某事）的。
note.usage: 形容詞，常用 be poised to V（即將…）或 be poised for + 名詞（為…做好準備）；新聞中常表示某事即將發生。

example.en: The team is poised to win its first championship in decades.
example.zh: 這支隊伍即將拿下數十年來的首座冠軍。

noteHi.usage: विशेषण: be poised to + क्रिया या be poised for + संज्ञा; समाचारों में आम।
noteHi.exampleTr: टीम दशकों में अपनी पहली चैंपियनशिप जीतने के लिए तैयार है।

noteEs.usage: Adjetivo: be poised to + verbo o be poised for + sustantivo; frecuente en noticias.
noteEs.exampleTr: El equipo está a punto de ganar su primer campeonato en décadas.

noteJa.meaning: （～する）態勢が整った、まさに～しようとしている。
noteJa.usage: 形容詞で be poised to do / be poised for ～ の形で使う。報道で「間もなく～する」の意味でよく使う。
noteJa.exampleTr: そのチームは数十年ぶりの優勝を目前にしている。

noteKo.usage: 형용사로 be poised to do / be poised for + 명사 형태로 씀. 뉴스에서 '곧 ~할 것'의 의미로 흔함.
noteKo.exampleTr: 그 팀은 수십 년 만의 첫 우승을 눈앞에 두고 있다.

noteEn.meaning: ready and about to do something.
noteEn.usage: Used as 'be poised to + verb' or 'be poised for + noun'; common in news.

prehistoric.en: from the time before written history
prehistoric.ex: The cave contains prehistoric paintings of animals.

prehistory.en: the time before written records existed
prehistory.ex: The museum shows tools from prehistory to today.

preservation.en: keeping something in its original state
preservation.ex: The group works for the preservation of old houses.

preserving.en: keeping something safe from harm or change
preserving.ex: Preserving the forest is important for wildlife.

price.en: the amount of money something costs (price tag)
price.ex: The price of rice went up this year.

professor.ex: The professor gave a talk about old buildings.

project.en: a large planned piece of work
project.ex: The bridge project will take five years.

proved.ex: The test proved harder than we expected.

pushed.ex: The storm pushed the opening back by a week.

qing.en: the Qing dynasty, which ruled China and Taiwan 1644–1912

railway.en: a track and system for trains
railway.ex: The railway runs along the coast.

ranging.en: covering a range between two points
ranging.ex: We sell shoes ranging from small to very large.

reach.en: to get to a number, level or stage
reach.ex: The project should reach its goal next year.

reading.en: the activity of reading books (reading areas/spaces)
reading.ex: The library has a quiet reading room upstairs.

reason.ex: The main reason for the delay was rain.

rebuilt.en: built again after damage or decay
rebuilt.ex: The bridge was rebuilt after the earthquake.

regarded.en: considered or thought of in a particular way
regarded.ex: She is regarded as the best player in the team.

relocating.en: moving something to a new place
relocating.ex: The company is relocating its office to the city centre.

remain.ja: とどまる；〜のままである
remain.en: to stay in the same place or condition
remain.ex: Please remain in your seats until the bus stops.

remains.en: objects or parts left from the past
remains.ex: Workers found the remains of an ancient wall.

removal.en: the act of taking something away
removal.ex: The removal of the old fence took two days.

remove.ex: The city will remove the old statues next month.

removed.ex: All the trees were removed from the car park.

repurposed.ja: 別の用途に転用される
repurposed.en: changed so it can be used for a new purpose
repurposed.ex: The old factory was repurposed as an art centre.

residents.en: people who live in a place
residents.ex: Local residents complained about the noise.

revealed.ex: The digging revealed an old well under the road.

ride.en: to travel on a bike or horse
ride.ex: My children ride their bikes to school.

road.en: a way for cars and other vehicles
road.ex: Be careful when you cross the road.

roughly.ex: The trip takes roughly two hours by car.

route.en: a way from one place to another
route.ex: This bus route goes past the hospital.

ruled.ex: The king ruled the country for forty years.

rules.en: official instructions about what is allowed
rules.ex: The new rules ban smoking in parks.

run.en: (of trains) to travel along a route
run.ex: Buses run every ten minutes in the morning.

running.ex: The trains will start running again at six.

safer.ex: Wide pavements make the street safer for children.

said.en: stated (past tense of say); (said yes = agreed)
said.ex: The teacher said the test was next week.

say.ex: Doctors say the new drug is safe.

says.ex: The report says sales fell last year.

schedule.en: a plan of when things will happen

scheduled.ex: The meeting is scheduled for Monday morning.

scheme.en: a large official plan or project
scheme.ex: The housing scheme will build 500 new homes.

section.ex: This section of the highway is closed today.

see.ex: You can see the mountains from my window.

seen.ex: The town has seen many changes this year.

serve.ex: The hall will serve as a school during repairs.

set.zh: 預定的（set to）；一組（a set of）
set.en: planned or expected (set to); a group of things (a set of)
set.ex: Prices are set to rise next month.

shops.ex: The shops close early on Sunday.

should.en: used to say what is right or expected
should.ex: You should drink more water every day.

shows.en: events where things are displayed (art shows)
shows.ex: The gallery holds two art shows every year.

sidelined.en: pushed aside and made less important
sidelined.ex: The old player was sidelined by younger stars.

significant.ex: This is a significant step for the company.

since.en: from a time in the past until now

sites.en: places used for a service; places with old remains
sites.ex: Workers found several ancient sites near the river.

small.ex: We ate lunch at a small cafe.

southern.ex: They live in a southern farming village.

souvenir.en: something bought to remember a place
souvenir.ex: I bought a souvenir mug in Tainan.

spaces.ex: The library has quiet spaces for study.

spanning.en: covering a period from one point to another
spanning.ex: The museum shows art spanning three centuries.

stage.en: one part or phase of a project
stage.ex: The first stage of the road is finished.

stand.en: be located or remain in a place
stand.ex: The old tree will stand beside the new house.

start.ex: Classes start at eight in the morning.

station.ex: We met at the train station.

stay.ex: The old bridge will stay open to walkers.

stop.ex: Cars must stop at the red light.

streets.en: public roads in a town or city
streets.ex: The streets were busy on Saturday night.

stretch.en: a continuous length of road or railway
stretch.ex: This stretch of road is very dangerous.

substantially.ex: Prices have risen substantially since last year.

sunken.en: built below the level of the ground around it
sunken.ex: Children played in the sunken garden.

superseded.ex: The old phone was superseded by a faster model.

note.meaning: 被取代、被替換（通常因較新或較好的事物）。
note.usage: supersede 的過去分詞，常用被動 be superseded by + 新事物。注意拼寫為 -sede 而非 -cede。

example.en: Paper maps have largely been superseded by smartphone apps.
example.zh: 紙本地圖已大多被智慧型手機應用程式取代。

noteHi.meaning: (नए या बेहतर द्वारा) प्रतिस्थापित किया गया।
noteHi.usage: supersede का भूतकृदंत; प्रायः be superseded by + संज्ञा। वर्तनी -sede है, -cede नहीं।
noteHi.exampleTr: काग़ज़ी नक़्शों की जगह अब अधिकतर स्मार्टफ़ोन ऐप्स ने ले ली है।

noteEs.meaning: sustituido, reemplazado (por algo más nuevo o mejor).
noteEs.usage: Participio de supersede; suele usarse como be superseded by + sustantivo. Se escribe -sede, no -cede.
noteEs.exampleTr: Los mapas de papel han sido en gran parte sustituidos por aplicaciones móviles.

noteJa.meaning: （より新しい物に）取って代わられた。
noteJa.usage: supersede の過去分詞。be superseded by ～ の受動態が多い。綴りは -sede（-cede ではない）。
noteJa.exampleTr: 紙の地図はスマートフォンのアプリにほぼ取って代わられた。

noteKo.usage: supersede의 과거분사. be superseded by + 명사 수동태가 흔함. 철자는 -sede(-cede 아님).
noteKo.exampleTr: 종이 지도는 대부분 스마트폰 앱으로 대체되었다.

noteEn.meaning: replaced by something newer or better.
noteEn.usage: Past participle of 'supersede'; often 'be superseded by + noun'. Spelled -sede.

surface.ex: The surface roads were closed for repairs.

swelled.ex: The crowd swelled to ten thousand people.

symbolic.en: having a special meaning that represents something
symbolic.ex: The new bridge is a symbolic link between towns.

tag.ex: The price tag on the car was too high.

taiwan.en: an island country in East Asia

taken.ex: The chairs were taken away after the party.

terminal.en: a large station for trains or buses
terminal.ex: The bus leaves from the main terminal.

then.ex: We met in 2010 and have been friends since then.

these.en: the ones here or just mentioned

this.en: the one here or just mentioned

those.en: the ones there or already mentioned

through.en: from one side to the other; (fall through the cracks) be missed

times.ex: People used stone tools in ancient times.

timetable.en: a plan showing when things will happen
timetable.ex: The project timetable was changed again.

today.en: on this day; at the present time

tracks.en: metal rails that trains run on
tracks.ex: Never walk on the railway tracks.

traffic.ex: Traffic is heavy in the morning.

trains.en: vehicles that run on railway tracks
trains.ex: The trains were late because of snow.

transformation.ex: The old port saw a big transformation.

transformed.ex: The factory was transformed into an art centre.

transport.en: systems for moving people or goods
transport.ex: Public transport here is cheap and fast.

transportation.en: moving people or goods (Ministry of Transportation)
transportation.ex: Good transportation helps the city grow.

turned.ex: The old school was turned into a hotel.

uncovered.ex: Farmers uncovered old coins in the field.

under.en: according to (under the plan); less than (under 50); below

underground.ex: The city built an underground car park.

university.ex: My sister studies at a university in Taipei.

up.en: to a higher level (go up); (free up) make available
up.ex: Food prices went up again this month.

urban.ex: Urban areas often have more traffic.

use.en: the act of using (in use: being used)
use.ex: The old bridge is still in use.

vacated.ex: The vacated office will become a cafe.

note.meaning: （被）騰出的、空出來的（空間、職位）。
note.usage: vacate 的過去分詞，可作形容詞放在名詞前（the vacated land / seat）；動詞 vacate a building / seat 表「搬離、讓出」。相關詞 vacant（空的）。

example.en: The vacated office space will be turned into classrooms.
example.zh: 騰出的辦公空間將改建為教室。

noteHi.usage: vacate का भूतकृदंत; संज्ञा से पहले विशेषण की तरह (the vacated land)। क्रिया: vacate a building।
noteHi.exampleTr: खाली किए गए कार्यालय स्थान को कक्षाओं में बदला जाएगा।

noteEs.meaning: desocupado, dejado libre (un espacio o cargo).
noteEs.usage: Participio de vacate; como adjetivo antes del sustantivo (the vacated land). Verbo: vacate a building.
noteEs.exampleTr: El espacio de oficinas desocupado se convertirá en aulas.

noteJa.meaning: 明け渡された、空いた（場所・地位）。
noteJa.usage: vacate の過去分詞。名詞の前で形容詞的に使う（the vacated land）。動詞 vacate a building（建物を明け渡す）。
noteJa.exampleTr: 空いたオフィススペースは教室に改装される。

noteKo.usage: vacate의 과거분사. 명사 앞에서 형용사처럼 씀(the vacated land). 동사 vacate a building(건물을 비우다).
noteKo.exampleTr: 비워진 사무 공간은 교실로 바뀔 것이다.

noteEn.meaning: left empty after people or things have moved out.
noteEn.usage: Past participle of 'vacate'; used before a noun ('the vacated corridor').

visitors.en: people who come to see a place
visitors.ex: The museum gets many visitors in summer.

walk.ex: I walk to school every morning.

walking.en: the activity of going on foot
walking.ex: Walking is good for your health.

was.ex: The station was very busy yesterday.

which.en: used to add information about a thing

wide.en: measuring a certain distance from side to side
wide.ex: The river is fifty metres wide here.

will.en: used to talk about the future
will.ex: The new bridge will open next year.

work.en: do a job or act together (v.); a job or a project (n.)
work.ex: Our teams work together on many projects.

workers.ex: The workers finished the bridge early.

year.ex: Last year we moved to Tainan.
